chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me of it, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ya'qub ibn Yaqtin, who said:

I asked Aba al-Hasan عليه السلام about a man who performed tayammum and prayed, then found water after his prayer: should he perform wudu (ablution) and repeat the salat (prayer), or is his prayer valid? He said: If he finds water before the time has passed, he performs wudu (ablution) and repeats; but if the time has passed, then there is no repetition upon him. And this report does not contradict that.

key_terms.الْوَقْتُ: the prescribed time of the prayer
key_terms.تَيَمَّمَ: performed tayammum, the dry ablution used in place of wudu (ablution) when water is unavailable
key_terms.فَلَا إِعَادَةَ عَلَيْهِ: there is no obligation upon him to repeat it

ai.seo_question: If someone prays with tayammum and then finds water, must the prayer be repeated?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who performed tayammum and then found water after completing salat (prayer). If water is found before the prayer time expires, he should perform wudu (ablution) and repeat the prayer; if the time has passed, no repetition is required.
